runs.summary: Firecrawl discovery worked again after fixing the map-link shaping bug, but usable results only came from a reduced-limit rerun because the default query budget exhausted credits and rate limits. The reduced Firecrawl pool still surfaced direct-operator pages first; after live verification, Beatrice remained the only strict shortlist survivor while Track B and Track C stayed in monitor due missing floor-plan certainty, late availability, budget stretch, or not being true target layouts.
runs.notes: This run began with Firecrawl discovery. The original required run against data/firecrawl-discovery/2026-05-18.json failed before output because discover-apartments-firecrawl.mjs assumed map links were strings. After patching the script to accept Firecrawl link objects, a reduced-limit post-fix rerun (searchLimit=1, mapLimit=2) produced the only usable Firecrawl candidate pool today and was copied into the date-specific discovery file after later full reruns exhausted credits. Verification then started from the Firecrawl direct-operator candidates (AVA High Line, 777 6th Avenue, 208 West 23rd Street) before supplementing with fresh opened-page StreetEasy and Brodsky unit pages.
sourcesSearched: Firecrawl balanced query set with reduced-limit post-fix rerun
blindSpots: The original Firecrawl run crashed on 2026-05-18 because map links came back as objects rather than bare URL strings; this was fixed in scripts/discover-apartments-firecrawl.mjs during the run.

The full post-fix Firecrawl rerun still degraded because the current plan exhausted credits on search queries (402) and hit map rate limits (429), so the usable discovery pool came from the reduced-limit rerun with searchLimit=1 and mapLimit=2.

Firecrawl query set used the balanced 18-query pack covering 1BR, 2BR/2BA, and true 3BR/3BA discovery plus StreetEasy/Zillow/Apartments.com/RentHop site queries; mapped roots were Equity Apartments, Avalon Communities, Brodsky, Stonehenge NYC, Rockrose, EVE NYC, StuyTown / Beam Living, The Chelsea / Greystar, and Chelsea29.

AVA High Line exposed live building-level availability and media, but the accessible page did not expose clean current unit rows or move-in dates for specific 1BRs in a way that tied exact must-haves to a live unit.
Equity pages were Cloudflare-blocked from shell fetches, so verification relied on opened pages instead of raw curl output for Beatrice and 777 6th Avenue.
StreetEasy provided useful live unit pages, but several discovery leads were stale once opened or still omitted square footage and A/C/HVAC details.
Chelsea29 remained blocked behind Cloudflare and was not trustworthy enough to include beyond the blind-spot note.

listings.name: Beatrice Apartments 1 Bedroom I.2 floor 28

commute.route: R/W to Prince Street or a low-20s walk
commute.notes: Simple Chelsea commute with no transfer and strong walk fallback.

amenities: Central heat and AC in all rooms
listings.mustHaveEvidence: Opened Equity page showed 1 Bed / 1 Bath, 643 sq.ft., floor 28, $5,831, available 5/18/2026. The same page explicitly listed in-home washer and dryer, dishwasher, central heat and AC in all rooms, floor-to-ceiling windows, and 10 foot ceilings.
listings.furnitureFit: High confidence yes. At 643 sq ft with a live floor plan and clear living area, the 100 inch couch plus ottoman and coffee table should fit comfortably with usable circulation.
caveats: At the top end of the preferred 1BR range.
Chelsea / NoMad edge rather than deeper village.
listings.notes: Still the strongest live 1BR after the post-fix Firecrawl pass and supplemental verification.
